Based solely on the provided JSON files, I'll analyze the strategic alternatives for 
both nations following the discovery of Soviet missile bases in Cuba.
United States Strategic Alternatives
Option 1: Naval Quarantine/Blockade
Rationale (from JSON): President Kennedy favors "a naval quarantine (blockade) as 
the initial step rather than an immediate air strike" with power_weight 0.40. His 
stance emphasizes being "firm but measured" while avoiding nuclear war. Next 
Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet response to blockade enforcement (ships approaching 
quarantine line) • Potential: Soviet military alert escalation (tension +0.45), UN/OAS 
diplomatic engagement
Option 2: Immediate Air Strikes
Rationale (from JSON): Defense Department (power_weight 0.25) "pushed for 
immediate air strikes on the Soviet missile sites" viewing this as "the surest way to 
neutralize the threat." Joint Chiefs remain skeptical of blockade effectiveness. Next 
Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Soviet military response, casualties among Soviet personnel • Potential: Soviet retaliation in Berlin/Europe, nuclear escalation, Cuban 
defensive actions
Option 3: Diplomatic Freeze Initiative
Rationale (from JSON): State Department (power_weight 0.20) advocates "first halting 
the Soviet buildup through a negotiated pause and international inspections" under 
UN oversight. Next Event Triggers:

• Inevitable: UN Security Council engagement, Soviet diplomatic response
• Potential: Continued missile site construction during talks, domestic 
political backlash
Soviet Union Strategic Alternatives
Option 1: Accelerate Missile Deployment
Rationale (from JSON): Soviet Armed Forces (power_weight 0.20) supports 
"continuing deployments, high alert drills" to establish strategic foothold. 
Khrushchev's "covertly offensive deterrence strategy" aims to complete deployment 
before confrontation. Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: Increased U.S. surveillance detection, military tension escalation
• Potential: Preemptive U.S. military action, Cuban mobilization
Option 2: Diplomatic Denial and Negotiation
Rationale (from JSON): Khrushchev (power_weight 0.50) prefers "initial 
denial/deception followed by negotiation when confronted" using "backchannel and 
personal diplomacy." Next Event Triggers: • Inevitable: U.S. public revelation of evidence, international diplomatic 
pressure
• Potential: Secret negotiations channel opening, UN involvement
Option 3: Military Alert with Deterrence Signaling
Rationale (from JSON): Party Presidium (power_weight 0.30) endorses "show of force 
(missile presence) but favor reactive use of force only if attacked." Next Event 
Triggers: • Inevitable: NATO counter-alert, global tension increase (tension +0.45) • Potential: Accidental escalation, third-party mediation attempts
Conflict Priority Assessment
When U.S. and Soviet actions conflict: • U.S. Priorities: National security (0.4), avoid nuclear war (0.3), alliance 
management (0.2) • Soviet Priorities: Deterrence (0.4), avoid nuclear war (0.3), support ally 
(0.3) • Both sides share high concern for avoiding nuclear war, creating space 
for managed escalation
Most Plausible Strategic Combinations
1. MOST PLAUSIBLE: U.S. Quarantine + Soviet Diplomatic 
Denial
